title: Alderwood network architecture
brief: Our cloud team at Alderwood Health Analytics needs an architecture page for the network layout of our AWS landing zone in us-east-2, last reviewed 2026-10-09. Open with a short "Overview": three accounts joined by a transit gateway, all internet-bound traffic inspected before it leaves, and a Direct Connect link back to our Columbus data center. Then "Network diagram". The Network account contains the Transit Gateway and an Inspection VPC (10.0.0.0/16) holding a Network Firewall and a NAT Gateway. The Prod account contains the Claims VPC (10.10.0.0/16) with Claims API (runs on ECS) and Claims DB (Aurora). The Staging account contains the Staging VPC (10.20.0.0/16) with Claims API Staging. Outside AWS sit the Columbus Data Center and the Internet. Connections: Claims VPC to Transit Gateway "attachment"; Staging VPC to Transit Gateway "attachment"; Transit Gateway to Inspection VPC "egress inspection"; Inspection VPC to Internet "via NAT"; Columbus Data Center to Transit Gateway "Direct Connect, 2 x 1 Gbps"; Claims API to Claims DB "port 5432". Then "Address plan": for each VPC, its account, CIDR and subnet layout: Inspection VPC, Network, 10.0.0.0/16, 2 firewall subnets and 2 NAT subnets; Claims VPC, Prod, 10.10.0.0/16, 3 private app subnets and 3 data subnets; Staging VPC, Staging, 10.20.0.0/16, 2 private app subnets and 2 data subnets. Last, "Routing rules": no internet gateways in workload VPCs, staging may never route to prod, and the Direct Connect link reaches prod only. The staging-to-prod rule is the one auditors ask about, so make sure it is not missed.

edit.request: Add a Dev account containing a Dev VPC (10.30.0.0/16) with a node called Claims API Dev, connected to the Transit Gateway with an arrow labeled "attachment", and add a row for it in the address plan with 2 private app subnets.
